# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Immediate action (today):**
- Call 3-5 of your best-performing coaches individually. Ask: "What do members ask you most about pricing? What confuses them?" Document exact phrases. Use these in your menu language—it'll resonate because it addresses real friction points.

**Structure it for TWO audiences simultaneously:**
- **Coach menu**: List every service tier with *exact* what-you-deliver specs (e.g., "Small Group (4-6 max, 45 min, 1:1 form check per person)" not just "Small Group Coaching"). Coaches need to know boundaries so they stop over-delivering or under-delivering.
- **Member menu**: Strip out internal jargon. Use outcome language instead ("Build strength + confidence" beats "Progressive resistance training"). Include what's bundled vs. à la carte—members hate surprise add-ons.

**Price architecture hack:**
- Anchor your premium offering first, then show "lite" versions below it. Psychology: members will trade down consciously rather than all anchor to your cheapest option. Test pricing on your 5 most-engaged members before publishing.

**Distribution format:**
- One-page PDF (print it—laminate copies for the gym floor). Pin to your website under a stupidly obvious button. Every new inquiry should receive this within 2 hours, auto-sent. This kills the "let me think about pricing" limbo.

**The real output:** You're not just listing services—you're eliminating decision paralysis for both coaches and prospects. That's where growth happens.

**Last 3 months (Jun–Aug) vs prior 3 (Mar–May):** Revenue fell from avg £15,382 to avg £17,363 — *but* membership grew 127→157 (+23.6%), yet revenue/member crashed from £124–£139 to £103–£124. **You are signing members but not collecting their full value.** August's £16,160 revenue on 157 members (£103/head) is the weakest unit economics in your dataset. This is your single biggest priority.

---

## 1. INCREASE REVENUE

• **Fix the collection leak immediately.** August: 157 active members should generate ~£19,250 at your Feb–Jul average (£122/member), but only brought £16,160. Check GoCardless/Stripe payment failures, declined cards, and late-paying card-only (non-DD) members in TeamUp. Recovery here alone could add £3,000/month.

• **Pricing hold + tier audit.** Your stable cohort (Feb, Jun, Jul) sits at £131–£145/member. You've grown headcount 37% (118→157 in 6 months) but revenue only 4% — new members are on cheaper tiers or are being admitted at discount. Audit current pricing tiers; enforce full-price entry for all new sign-ups from September. Target: stabilise at £135/member minimum = £21,200/month at 157 members.

• **Churn spike in May (12.8%) killed momentum.** You've since recovered (3.4%–8.1%), but lost ~15 members that month. Root cause: post-relocation or pricing sensitivity? Identify and plug. Current 5.6–8.1% is acceptable but 10%+ annually is a ~50-member bleed. Implement exit surveys; offer 1-month freeze (not refund) for at-risk members.

• **Upsell PT/classes on induction.** No data on ancillary revenue. At 157 members, even 20% uptake at £40/month (e.g. 4 PT sessions or unlimited classes) adds £1,260/month. Assign induction script and track PT/class add-ons in TeamUp.
